designs.title: Belize
designs.why: A clean one-ink job: the alpha is hard-edged (no partial pixels), there are no specks under 9 px, and most strokes are 4-6 px (0.35-0.5 mm), which holds on a 156-160 mesh. The scene reads at 3 m (palms, hut, a jetty running into the frame, coral patches as dark masses) and fits the tee at roughly 28 cm wide. The type is solid and the coordinates are big enough (about 6 mm caps). The one weak spot is the machine crosshatch tint on the pilings, the hut walls and under the dock: its reversed holes are only about 4-5 px (around 0.4 mm), so with plastisol on ringspun they will half-plug into blotchy grey patches. They look different from the hand-cut linework around them and are the only part that will print unevenly from shirt to shirt. The empty gap between the BELIZE rule and the treetops is generous but works as breathing room.
designs.fix: Remove the crosshatch tint patches and redraw those shadows as solid ink or open hand hatching, keeping the white gaps at least 0.5 mm (6 px at 300 DPI), so every shadow prints the same and matches the engraved linework.
